title: orders-db write latency spike after a deploy — a lock storm, or replication backpressure from the standby?

ground_truth.summary: Deploy v6.02.0 introduced a long-running transaction that holds row locks on orders-db; lock-wait climbs first and sustains, throttling writes and cascading into checkout 5xx. The standby replica's replication-lag blip at 10:00:40 was a brief, self-recovering catch-up after the deploy restart — a coincidence, not the lead. Rolling back the deploy removes the offending transaction and restores writes.

observables.name: lock_wait_time
observables.desc: time write transactions spend waiting on row locks in orders-db

observables.desc: orders-db-standby replication lag behind the primary

seed_hypotheses.claim: The 10:00 deploy introduced a long-running transaction that holds row locks, causing write contention on orders-db.

predicted_observations.note: lock-wait leads the write-latency and 5xx rise if a held lock is the cause

seed_hypotheses.claim: The standby replica's replication lag caused upstream commit backpressure that cascaded into checkout write failures.

predicted_observations.note: if replication backpressure leads, lock-wait is a downstream symptom that lags
standby lag leads the whole stall

prior._note_for_authors: THE TRAP for the change agent: a recent deploy 8 min before the alert.

files.hunk:
-    with db.begin():
-        settle_batch(rows)
+    with db.begin():
+        for row in rows:
+            settle_and_audit(row)  # holds the txn open across the whole batch

prior._note_for_authors: THE TRAP: a brief replication-lag spike at 10:00:40 (240ms) that RECOVERS to ~58ms. It is EARLIER than the sustained signals, so a cascade story (H2) looks plausible from prior alone — but it is transient (a post-deploy catch-up), not a sustained lead. The discriminator (lock-wait ordering) must live only in probeable.

payload.signature: long transaction holds row locks; lock-wait and write latency climb after a deploy
payload.resolution: Rolled back the deploy that opened a batch-wide transaction; lock-wait cleared.

probeable._note_for_authors: THE DISCRIMINATOR. lock-wait sustains a rise from 10:01:30 — BEFORE write-latency (10:03:30) and long before the replication blip recovers. It leads sustainedly → confirms H1 (rises_first) and falsifies H2 (rises_later). Present in probeable only.

Low-value distractor. Standby replication has recovered and is flat — consistent with the blip being benign — but it does not resolve the ordering question, so its info-gain is lower than P_lock_wait.
